newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods prices seen lower amid APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods prices seen lower amid APIs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices were lower Tuesday amid reports showing a build in regional gasoline inventories, traders said.
Sellers lowered spot prices early to try to draw out buyers waiting on Tuesday's inventory data. Meanwhile, NYMEX levels ended weaker on Tuesday.
The American Petroleum Institute (API), a Washington D.C. -based trade group, showed West Coast supplies of gasoline rose 623,000 barrels last week to 29.5 million barrels.
Traders said inventories built at supply terminals because poor weather in recent weeks has lowered motorist demand.
Offers for CARB mandated Phase II reformulated gasoline remained 77.50 cents.
CARB grade diesel oil in L.A. stayed 73/74.50 cents after trimming a half cent early, traders said.
San Francisco gasoline remained two cents under L.A. prices as demand remained static after heavy rains early this month.
